Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a single complete modular city building sprite for a Cocos2D game. The attached approved HOME image is ONLY the painting, architectural quality, materials, color and daylight reference, NOT a request to redraw its UI or whole city. Produce ONE beautifully designed finished building, native transparent RGBA, square canvas, building fully visible with safe transparent margins. Faithfully match the bright, refined Japanese urban anime painted architecture in that reference: crisp warm ivory stone, fine architectural detailing, natural blue-grey reflective glass, charcoal metalwork, warm orange accents, subtle wear, rich but controlled painterly shading, no blue cast over everything. Strict orthographic oblique camera: look DOWN from elevation 30 degrees, two visible facade ground edges each rise at 30 degrees toward left/right, verticals remain vertical, no horizon/vanishing point, no exaggerated wide-angle. Fixed screen-upper-left warm sunlight; coherent shaded side and window reveals; no external cast ground shadow (engine will add it). NO detached base platform, no surrounding pavement, no road, no trees on roof, no UI/text/logo/watermark, no people/vehicles, no full scene, no 3D plastic toy or low-poly style. Building occupies ~86% canvas width. Entire lowest front ground corner around center x=.50, y=.92 with clear wall-ground contact. Rectangular compact footprint about 9m x 9m, not a thin tower. No attached tall plants or benches extending footprint.
Subject: A sophisticated lively THREE-storey corner cafe/restaurant. Refined ivory facade with staggered volumes and a modest recessed upper balcony, carefully arranged large glazing, slim dark bronze frames. On the STREET FRONT put a double glass entrance with clearly readable door handles, adjacent cafe windows, and elegant orange fabric awnings with believable brackets. Ground-floor interior suggests warm cafe counters and chairs; upper storeys have well-composed grouped windows. Small metal handrail details and subtle cornices. No rooftop trees or bright emissive halo.
Critical frontage direction: The PUBLIC STREET is to the SCREEN LOWER-RIGHT of this building. The MAIN FRONT facade is the visible RIGHT-HAND face (the face on the viewer's right); put the unambiguous main entrance and canopy centered ON THAT RIGHT FACE, halfway between lowest front corner and right ground corner. The visible LEFT face is a secondary quieter side with windows, NO public main doorway. Do not put the door on the left facade.
